terms.comment: To straighten what has gone crooked: a mistake (mendum, peccātum, errōrem corrigere), a text, a person. Traupman: of a person or of a mistake (p. 29).

terms.gloss: correct (a text, a piece of work), free from mistakes
terms.comment: Of written work: the teacher corrects his pupils’ writing (ut scrīptūram vestram ēmendem, Vives, Exerc. 10); see also improve. Correction is ēmendātiō or corrēctiō (Traupman 29).

phrases.latin: Quīntiliō sī quid recitārēs, «corrige, sōdēs, hoc» ajēbat «et hoc».
phrases.english: If you read anything out to Quintilius, he would say, “Correct this, please, and this.”

phrases.latin: at ūnus certē sit assiduus loquendī nōn imperītus, quī, sī qua erunt ab hīs praesente alumnō dicta vitiōsē, corrigat prōtinus nec īnsīdere illī sinat
phrases.english: at least let there be one person always at hand who speaks well, to correct at once anything the others say wrongly in the child’s hearing, and not let it settle in him
